headline: Council passed a rent control resolution 7-2, appropriated $386,037 for Hope House rehabilitation, approved several grants, and amended Fore Street traffic rules.
summary: The council approved appointments to the Casco Bay Trail Board, outdoor dining for Terlingua LLC, and an EMS Transport Plan. It passed an amended resolution on rent control and tenant protections 7-2 after extensive public comment, approved $386,037 for Hope House rehabilitation, a MaineDOT intersection agreement, several grants including $73,721, $20,000, and $151,500, an opioid settlement funds code amendment, and a Fore Street traffic schedule change. Two EPA Brownfields funding orders of $500,000 and $1,000,000 received only a first reading.
decisions: Appointed members to the Casco Bay Trail Board of Supervisors for 2026, passage 9-0.
Granted Terlingua LLC, dba The Terlingua Outpost, approval for outdoor dining on public property at 34 Washington Avenue, passage 9-0.
Adopted the Emergency Medical Services Transport Plan, passage 9-0.

Passed, as amended, the resolution to fully enforce rent control, strengthen tenant protections, and guarantee safe and stable housing for renters, 7-2, with Councilor Phillips and Mayor Dion opposed.
Adopted Sykes Amendment 1 to Resolve 2-26/27, passage 7-2, with Councilor Phillips and Mayor Dion opposed.
Mayor Amendment 2 to Resolve 2-26/27 failed, 4-5, with Councilors Fournier, Grant, Sykes, Pelletier and Bullett opposed.
Councilor Pelletier's floor motion to amend Resolve 2-26/27 failed for lack of a second.
Appropriated $386,037 from the Jill C. Duson Housing Trust Fund to Hope Acts for Hope House Rehabilitation, passage 9-0.
Approved the agreement between the Maine Department of Transportation and Portland for improvements to State Street, High Street, and Forest Avenue at fourteen intersections, passage 9-0.
Accepted and appropriated a $73,721 United States Department of Justice grant, passage 9-0.

Approved the service contract with the State of Maine Health and Human Services Department and accepted $20,000 in additional grant funding for Victim and Witness Advocacy Services, passed as an emergency, 9-0.
Passed the amendment to Portland City Code Chapter 2 regarding Opioid Settlement Funds, passage 9-0.
Approved the Traffic Schedule Amendment for Fore Street, 8-1, with Councilor Sykes opposed.
Accepted and appropriated a $151,500 grant revenue award from Workforce & Enterprise Operations to the Portland Jetport TSA K9 Unit, passed as an emergency, 8-1, with Councilor Sykes opposed.
Waived the second reading for Order 37-26/27, passage 8-1, with Councilor Sykes opposed.
